key_insight: Zero-shot large language models, especially Gemini 3.5 Flash, extracted colorectal cancer symptoms from discharge notes more accurately than rule-based and clinical NER approaches.
clinical_relevance: This suggests LLM-based note mining could scale symptom surveillance in oncology without building site-specific rules or training models.
method: Analyzed 2,704 CRC discharge notes from MIMIC-IV
Benchmarked rule-based matching, clinical NER, Claude Haiku, and Gemini 3.5 Flash
Compared against a 200-note adjudicated gold standard with macro/micro F1, precision, and recall
evidence_signal: On the gold-standard evaluation set, Gemini 3.5 Flash achieved Macro F1 0.70 and Micro F1 0.86, outperforming rule-based (Macro F1 0.44) and NER (Macro F1 0.38) methods.
watch_item: Post-hoc negation filtering reduced LLM performance, highlighting the need for syntactic scope-aware validation before deployment.
paper_title: Leveraging Large Language Models for Colorectal Cancer Symptom Extraction from MIMIC-IV Clinical Notes
